summary: Extends the VPLS provider edge model to work with IEEE 802.1 Provider Backbone Bridging. PBB scales better than Provider Bridges in customer MAC addresses and service instances, and this document explains how VPLS can extend such services across an MPLS backbone.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 7041 describes how Provider Backbone Bridging can be used inside VPLS provider-edge devices. This lets the backbone carry grouped customer traffic using provider-level addresses and service instances.

subtitle: Combining PBB with VPLS to reduce backbone service state

tldr.problem: A VPLS core can need many customer MAC addresses and pseudowires as customer services grow. This document explains how Provider Backbone Bridging can reduce that state.
tldr.mechanism: PBB wraps customer Ethernet frames in provider addressing and service identifiers. VPLS pseudowires then carry backbone service instances rather than each customer service separately.
tldr.outcome: RFC 7041 describes a PBB-VPLS provider-edge architecture and reuse of existing VPLS signaling. It is informational, not a protocol specification.

facts.label: VPLS role
facts.value: A VPLS instance represents a backbone service instance

today: RFC 7041 is an Informational document and the batch metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it. It describes an architecture for combining PBB and VPLS, not a new signaling protocol.

sections.title: Why Combine PBB and VPLS
sections.content:
Virtual Private LAN Service (VPLS) carries Ethernet LAN services across a routed Multiprotocol Label Switching (MPLS) backbone. In ordinary VPLS, provider-edge devices learn customer MAC addresses and maintain pseudowires for customer service instances, which can become difficult to manage as the number of services grows.

Provider Backbone Bridges (PBB) add a hierarchy: customer frames are carried inside provider-addressed frames, and a service identifier associates each frame with its provider service. RFC 7041 describes how to combine PBB with VPLS while avoiding a native Ethernet control protocol across the MPLS backbone.
sections.plainLanguage: VPLS carries customer Ethernet traffic across an MPLS network. PBB groups customer traffic under provider addressing, reducing what the backbone must track.

sections.title: The PBB-VPLS Provider Edge
sections.content:
A PBB bridge has customer-facing I-components and provider-facing B-components. An I-component bridges customer MAC addresses and service VLAN information. A B-component bridges provider backbone MAC addresses and backbone VLANs.

In the extended provider-edge model, the PBB bridge module connects to VPLS forwarders. A VPLS instance represents a backbone service instance, and its pseudowires connect the provider-edge devices. Multiple customer services can be mapped to a backbone service instance, reducing the number of pseudowires and customer MAC addresses handled in the core.
sections.plainLanguage: The provider edge receives customer frames, adds PBB provider information, and connects the result to VPLS pseudowires. The backbone can carry several customer services within a backbone service instance.

sections.title: How a Frame Crosses the Backbone
sections.content:
A customer frame reaches an I-component with its customer MAC addresses and VLAN information. The PBB bridge encapsulates it with provider backbone addresses, a backbone VLAN tag, and an I-tag identifying the service instance. A pseudowire forwarder maps the service to an MPLS pseudowire for transport.

At the receiving provider edge, the forwarder removes the pseudowire and packet-switched-network encapsulation. The B-component forwards by provider destination MAC; when the frame goes toward a customer, the I-component removes the provider encapsulation and bridges using the customer destination MAC. Unknown and group destinations may be flooded to the applicable destinations.
sections.plainLanguage: The provider edge wraps a customer frame with provider addressing and a service identifier. The far edge removes that wrapping and delivers the customer frame.

sections.title: Signaling, Replication, and OAM
sections.content:
PBB-VPLS reuses existing VPLS procedures for pseudowire setup, auto-discovery, and signaling. Hierarchical VPLS may be used in customer or backbone service instances. The architecture also reuses existing VPLS features to improve packet replication and describes applying multicast snooping and Multiple MAC Registration Protocol where appropriate.

Existing VPLS, pseudowire, MPLS, and PBB OAM procedures may be used to check connectivity components. The document states that it introduces no security issues beyond those described in the base VPLS RFCs.
sections.plainLanguage: The design reuses existing VPLS signaling and OAM tools. RFC 7041 says its security considerations are covered by the underlying VPLS specifications.
